clue.text: See 4
Why said boozer is among places for those who like to indulge

indicators.note: something that is among other things sits within them, so these letters go inside the word for places

parts.note: places are sites

indicators.note: said points to how a word sounds, so the letter that sounds like the word why is wanted

parts.note: the word why sounds like the letter Y
a boozer is British slang for a pub, so a bar

explanation.surface: A drinker turns up in the haunts of pleasure-seekers, which is hardly a surprise.
explanation.definitionFit: Sybarites, after the luxurious ancient city of Sybaris, are people devoted to pleasure and self-indulgence.

clue.text: Copy letter in delight

indicators.note: in places the Greek letter inside the word for delight

parts.note: to delight someone is to elate them
mu is a letter of the Greek alphabet

explanation.surface: An instruction to reproduce a letter while feeling joyful.
explanation.definitionFit: To emulate someone is to imitate them, matching or copying what they do.

clue.text: Polynesian artist grabbing a paintbrush at last

indicators.note: grabbing means the painter's name holds the other letters within it

parts.note: Titian was the Venetian Renaissance painter

indicators.note: at last picks the final letter of the word paintbrush

explanation.surface: A Polynesian painter finally reaches for a brush, as Gauguin's island subjects might have.
explanation.definitionFit: A Tahitian is a native of Tahiti, an island of French Polynesia, so a Polynesian person.

clue.text: There may be two edits then, corrected after the girl gets drunk

indicators.note: after means the rearranged edits come behind the girl
may be suggests the word There could become another arrangement of its letters

parts.note: the girl is she

indicators.note: corrected means the words two edits then are fixed into a new order

explanation.surface: An editor's note: there could be two corrections, made after the woman has had too much to drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'corrected' reads like proofreading, but it is the anagram signal, as is 'may be'; 'after' fixes the order, so the girl comes first. The phrase is a sailing idiom: a ship with loose sheets (ropes) staggers.
explanation.definitionFit: Three sheets to the wind is a sailing idiom for being very drunk, like a ship with its sheets loose.

clue.text: In days gone by, receiving only television's first channel

indicators.note: receiving means the word for long ago takes the other letters inside it

parts.note: in days gone by means then, at that past time
only means sole, as in the sole survivor

indicators.note: first picks the opening letter of television's

explanation.surface: Nostalgia for the era when there was a single TV channel to watch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'channel' looks like TV, but it is a sea channel: The Solent is the strait between the Isle of Wight and the English mainland.
explanation.definitionFit: The Solent is a strait, a stretch of water linking two seas, and a strait is also called a channel.

clue.text: Old money does badly, if copper is involved

indicators.note: is involved means the metal's symbol is wrapped up inside the jumbled letters
badly means the letters of does are put together wrongly, in a new order

parts.note: Cu is the chemical symbol for copper

explanation.surface: A warning that old cash performs poorly when it includes copper coins.
explanation.walkthrough: 'badly' scrambles does and 'is involved' wraps that scramble round the chemical symbol for copper.
explanation.definitionFit: The escudo was the currency of Portugal until the euro replaced it, so a former money.

clue.text: Possible property holding in quaint, rustic setting

indicators.note: in tells the solver the letters are found within the next words
setting means the words quaint rustic surround and hold the letters, as a ring holds a stone

explanation.surface: An estate agent's line about a property for sale in a charming country spot.
explanation.definitionFit: Property can be held in trust, managed by trustees for a beneficiary, so that is one possible form of holding it.

clue.text: Guys overwhelmed by debts start to default

indicators.note: overwhelmed by means the first letter is swamped, sitting inside the word for debts

parts.note: debts are dues, sums owed

indicators.note: start to picks the first letter of default

explanation.surface: Men buried under money owed begin to fail on their payments.
explanation.definitionFit: Dudes is informal slang for men or fellows, just as guys is.

clue.text: Boots' foremost more luxurious make-up

indicators.note: foremost picks the opening letter of Boots'

parts.note: lush means luxurious, so more luxurious is lusher

explanation.surface: Boots, the British high-street chemist, has a premium cosmetics line.
explanation.walkthrough: Boots is a UK chain of chemist shops that sells cosmetics.
explanation.definitionFit: Blusher is a cosmetic, rouge applied to the cheeks, so an example of make-up.

clue.text: Charlie left outside in a tizzy

indicators.note: outside means the word for left goes round the letter

parts.note: left means exited, departed
Charlie is C in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: Charlie has been shut out and is in a flap about it.
explanation.definitionFit: Being in a tizzy means being in a state of nervous agitation, so excited.

clue.text: Midsummer Day ends with a group of sailors

indicators.note: ends picks the last letter of each of Midsummer and Day

explanation.surface: Midsummer's Day closes with a gathering of seafarers.
explanation.definitionFit: The RYA is the Royal Yachting Association, the UK governing body for boating and sailing.

clue.text: Quiet period for percussion, around 50 cents?

indicators.note: around means the drums enclose the fifty-cent piece

parts.note: percussion in a band is the drums
fifty cents is half a dollar, so half of the word dollar, its first three letters

explanation.surface: A lull in drumming, paid for with a little small change.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags the playful step: 50 cents is half a dollar, so half the word DOLLAR.
explanation.definitionFit: The doldrums is an idiom for a spell of stagnation or inactivity, from the calm ocean belt near the equator.

clue.text: See 20
A Philistine in church? Christmas must be coming up for one so fickle

parts.note: Philistine is the setter of this puzzle, so the setter refers to themself as me

indicators.note: coming up in a down clue means the word for Christmas is read from bottom to top

parts.note: Noel is another word for Christmas

explanation.surface: The setter turns up in church only because Christmas is approaching, a fair-weather worshipper.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A Philistine' is the setter's own byline: the setter is ME.
explanation.definitionFit: A chameleon changes colour to match its surroundings, so figuratively it is a changeable or inconstant person.

clue.text: See 18
Got hold of shank?

definitions.meaning: got hold of someone means reached or communicated with them, as by phone
in golf a shank is a mishit in which the ball is struck by the hosel, the neck of the club; the question mark flags the loose sense of the club meeting the ball

explanation.definitionFit: Getting hold of someone is reaching them by phone or letter, the everyday sense of making contact.

clue.text: Like minor German and European furore

parts.note: und is the German word for and
a furore is a rage, an angry craze

explanation.surface: A minor in Germany and Europe causes uproar.
explanation.definitionFit: A minor is someone not yet of legal age, so the adjective describing that person is underage.

clue.text: Symbolic house of the listener?

parts.note: a semi is a semi-detached house, the common British home sharing one wall
otic means relating to the ear, the listener's organ

explanation.surface: A house that stands as an emblem of the person listening.
explanation.walkthrough: A semi is a semi-detached house, very common in Britain.
explanation.definitionFit: Semiotic means relating to signs and symbols and how they carry meaning.

clue.text: Kimonos may be useful on the slopes of Mount Fuji

definitions.text: Kimonos may be useful on the slopes of Mount Fuji

indicators.note: may be suggests the letters of Kimonos could form another word in a new order

explanation.surface: Japanese robes might come in handy for skiing on Mount Fuji.
explanation.walkthrough: 'may be' rearranges KIMONOS; the whole clue then describes the answer as something handy on a Japanese ski slope.
explanation.definitionFit: A monoski is a single broad ski used with both feet, so equipment used on snowy slopes.

clue.text: Regularly abreast, saving time for the news? Drink up and get ready for the worst

indicators.note: saving here means keeping, so the alternate letters hold the rest inside them
regularly picks every other letter of abreast, the second, fourth and sixth

parts.note: at ten, ten o'clock being the hour of a British evening news bulletin
down the hatch is the toast urging a drinker to swallow

explanation.surface: Keeping up with the news, then a stiff drink before preparing for a storm.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Regularly' takes alternate letters of abreast and 'saving' holds the rest within them. The BBC's flagship evening news has long gone out at ten o'clock.
explanation.definitionFit: Battening down the hatches is securing a ship before a storm, so figuratively preparing for trouble.

clue.text: Terrestrial radiophones not paid off

indicators.note: not says the letters of paid are excluded from the larger word
off means the remaining letters are thrown out of order and rearranged

explanation.surface: Earthbound radio telephones that haven't been fully paid for.
explanation.walkthrough: Take PAID's letters out of RADIOPHONES ('not'), leaving ROHONES, which 'off' rearranges.
explanation.definitionFit: Onshore means on land rather than at sea, so terrestrial in the sense of belonging to the land.

clue.text: Scruffy label on scruffy item of clothing

indicators.note: on means the word for label goes onto the end of the clothing word

parts.note: a rag is a worn-out, tattered garment
a tag is a label

explanation.surface: An untidy tag stitched onto a tatty garment.
explanation.definitionFit: Ragtag means untidy, disorganised or motley, as a ragtag band of followers.

clue.text: Flipping competition car reverses, breaking a kneecap in bits

indicators.note: breaking means the turned car word bursts into the middle of the jumbled kneecap
in bits means a kneecap is smashed into pieces and reassembled in another order
reverses means the word car is read backwards

explanation.surface: A car accident: the vehicle backs up and smashes someone's kneecap to pieces.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flipping' looks like a mild oath but it is the definition: pancake races, a British Shrove Tuesday tradition, have runners tossing pancakes as they go.
explanation.definitionFit: A pancake race is run while tossing a pancake in a pan, so a contest involving flipping.

clue.text: Naval administrator in picture frame turned spy

indicators.note: frame picks the outer letters of picture, its border
turned means the letters of spy are rearranged

explanation.surface: A navy official, pictured in a frame, has become a spy.
explanation.definitionFit: Samuel Pepys, the diarist, was a senior official of the Admiralty, a naval administrator under Charles II and James II.

clue.text: Manoeuvre fails to start in range

indicators.note: fails to start means the word loses its first letter

parts.note: a gambit is an opening manoeuvre, as in chess

explanation.surface: A tactic that never gets off the ground, within reach.
explanation.definitionFit: Ambit means scope or extent, the bounds within which something operates.

clue.text: Environment suitable for tailless mammal

indicators.note: tailless means the word loses its final letter

parts.note: a seal is a marine mammal

explanation.surface: A habitat suited to an animal that has lost its tail.
explanation.definitionFit: The sea is a surrounding medium in which creatures live, so an environment or habitat.

clue.text: Be lavish and encourage the snake promoter

parts.note: to push is to urge or encourage
a boa is a constricting snake
a tout touts goods or tickets, promoting them noisily

explanation.surface: Spending freely while backing someone who sells snakes.
explanation.definitionFit: To push the boat out is a British idiom for spending generously on a celebration.

clue.text: See 26
He dealt poorly with non-monogamous behaviour, being lazy

parts.note: swinging is couples swapping partners

indicators.note: poorly means the letters of He dealt are put together badly, in a new order

explanation.surface: Someone who handled a partner-swapping situation badly.
explanation.definitionFit: Swinging the lead is British slang for shirking work by feigning illness, originally a sailors' phrase.
